Lack of reported skin/nail changes, dactylitis, or enthesitis reduces—but does not exclude—psoriatic arthritis. Ankylosing spondylitis is included given its potential for peripheral arthritis (especially wrist/knee involvement in early or non-radiographic forms) and prolonged stiffness, though axial symptoms are not yet elicited. SLE is plausible due to chronic symmetric arthralgia/arthritis (often non-erosive, non-deforming) and frequent absence of swelling; however, absence of other systemic features (rash, photosensitivity, renal, hematologic) lowers confidence. Chronic inflammatory myopathy is lower-confidence because proximal muscle weakness and elevated CK would typically dominate over isolated joint pain—but overlap syndromes (e.g., anti-synthetase syndrome) can present with prominent arthralgias and stiffness mimicking RA. Fibromyalgia is deliberately excluded: while it causes widespread pain and fatigue, it does not cause objectively prolonged inflammatory morning stiffness (>30 min) — that feature is highly specific for immune-mediated synovitis. Diagnostic uncertainty reflects moderate dispersion across plausible autoimmune rheumatic conditions pending further evaluation (e.g., RF/ACPA, HLA-B27, psoriasis exam, CRP/ESR, imaging)."}
